## 1. psf/requests #7413: Fix HTTPDigestAuth uri field truncated by semicolons in URL path
- Repo: https://github.com/psf/requests
- PR: https://github.com/psf/requests/pull/7413 by zons-zhaozhy, last updated 2026-10-28 05:17 IST (2026-10-27T23:47:40Z), mergeable clean
- Head: 418c76b8aa7be2255ecd2d045f761e6411ba0acb
- Base: 04d750509b90da728e53aee8d7516426e5a1a293 (main; = merge base, 1 ahead, 0 behind)
- Claims: for URLs with `;params` in the path, `HTTPDigestAuth.build_digest_header()` dropped the params from the Digest `uri=` field, so servers that check the full request URI reject the login (issue #6990, MusicBrainz). Now `;params` is kept. Changes src/requests/auth.py (2+), one test in tests/test_lowlevel.py.
- Expected verdict: **verified.** Local probe: `https://h/ws/2/artist;name=Nirvana` gives uri `/ws/2/artist` on base and `/ws/2/artist;name=Nirvana` on head; `https://h/a;b?q=1` gives `/a?q=1` vs `/a;b?q=1`. Unchanged both sides: `/a?q=1`, `https://h/` and `https://h` give `/`.
- Watch: tests/test_lowlevel.py had 8 failures on BOTH sides on the local (`test_use_proxy_from_environment[...]`, proxy environment of the sandbox); base 12 passed, head 13 passed. Those must not be read as PR breaks. The new test alone: `-k digest` 4 passed on head.
- Setup: pure Python, no build. Deps urllib3 idna charset_normalizer certifi (pure wheels). `PYTHONPATH=src pytest tests/test_lowlevel.py -o addopts=""` (about 56 s, proxy tests are slow) or faster subset `-k "digest or Digest"`. Install size: small.

## 2. Textualize/rich #3163: Swap open-vs-close tag order when converting Text to markup
- Repo: https://github.com/Textualize/rich
- PR: https://github.com/Textualize/rich/pull/3163 by slaarti, last updated 2026-10-30 02:19 IST (2026-10-29T20:49:24Z; PR itself is from Nov 2023), mergeable clean
- Head: cab14dbbe325fa387ec056ba199e5f1f3a18688a
- Base: 50d2a457c8ea273c14a0053b00493473b86dbe21 (main field; = merge base, 7 ahead, 0 behind; the base commit is old, Nov 2023)
- Claims: `Text.markup` put opening tags before closing tags at the same offset, so `[red]foo[/red][blue]bar[/blue]` came back as `[red]foo[blue][/red]bar...`; now closing tags come first and that round-trips exactly (fixes #3155). Changes rich/text.py (6+/6-), one test, changelog. The author says it may be "too simple to possibly be correct".
- Expected verdict: **needs attention (real break found pre-pick).** The claimed fix works: the adjacent-tags example round-trips exactly on head (base gives the interleaved form, which still re-parses to the same spans). But zero-length spans now produce markup that cannot be parsed: `Text.from_markup("a[red][/red]b").markup` is `a[red][/red]b` on base and `a[/red][red]b` on head, and `Text.from_markup` of the head output raises `MarkupError: closing tag '[/red]' ... doesn't match any open tag`. Same for `"[red][/red]"`, `"x[bold]y[/bold][red][/red]z"`, and for `Text("ab").append_text(Text("", style="red"))`. Base re-parses all of these.
- Watch: a true-catch case like python-barcode #162: a tool that only probes the claimed adjacent-tag input will wrongly say verified. Tests: `tests/test_text.py tests/test_markup.py` base 121 passed 2 failed, head 122 passed 2 failed; the 2 failures (`test_render`, `test_no_wrap_no_crop`) fail on both sides on the local (environment), not PR breaks. The repo tests do not cover zero-length spans, so the break shows only in probes.
- Setup: pure Python (poetry-core). Deps pygments markdown-it-py. `PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/test_text.py tests/test_markup.py -o addopts=""` (under 1 s). Install size: small.
